subject: Information Theory
title: Recommendation Algorithms
description: A quick, practical guide to Recommendation Algorithms.

hook.text: Netflix's algorithm saved the company $1 billion per year by recommending shows you'd actually watch.

buildup.text: Recommendation systems predict preferences by analyzing patterns: what people like you watched, bought, or clicked.

discovery.text: Collaborative filtering compares user behavior. Content-based filtering analyzes item features. Hybrids combine both.

twist.text: Recommendations create filter bubbles. You see more of what you've already consumed, narrowing your information space.

climax.text: The information-theoretic tension: personalization reduces entropy of your feed while maximizing predicted engagement.

punchline.text: Show them what they'll like. Slowly, they see nothing else.

quiz.question: What information-theoretic effect do recommendation algorithms create?
options: They reduce entropy by narrowing the information space
